sections.h2: Where an Anderson County deed gets recorded
sections.html:
Deeds for Anderson County land are recorded at the County Clerk's counter, 100 S Main St, Lawrenceburg, KY 40342. Recording is what protects the buyer against later purchasers who had no notice and against the seller's creditors (KRS 382.110(1)).

Lawrenceburg is the seat and the only city. Most sellers never walk the deed in themselves. The closing office carries the signed original to the clerk, pays the fees, and gets the stamped deed back later. Even if the lender or title agent sits in Franklin, Woodford or Shelby County, the filing still lands in Lawrenceburg, because the county where the land lies controls.

sections.h2: What must be written into the deed
sections.html:
KRS 382.135 bars the clerk from accepting a deed that leaves out certain items. A quick review before the closing saves a second trip.

  • Full names and mailing addresses for both grantor and grantee.
  • A statement of the entire consideration.
  • An in-care-of address showing where that year's tax bill should go.
  • A notarized, sworn certificate signed for both sides confirming that the price shown is everything paid. A gift deed carries a certificate saying it is a gift, with an estimated fair cash value.

KRS 382.110 adds a title-source rule. The deed names the earlier deed by office, book, page and recording date, or explains how the seller acquired the land if it came through inheritance. When a house passed under a will, or with none, an affidavit from the estate's personal representative is also needed. It is filed before the estate closes and names each person who received property, each parcel and its value.

The posted fee schedule took effect January 1, 2020. Each page after the fifth adds $3, and for mortgages the $3 begins after page thirty. Kentucky also charges a separate $4 tax on each real property conveyance under KRS 142.010, which the clerk collects and passes along. Ask whether a quoted total already includes it.

A seller typically pays for a deed and perhaps a release, so clerk charges make up a small part of closing costs.

sections.h2: How the state transfer tax works
sections.html:
The seller pays $0.50 for each $500 of value stated in the deed, and a leftover partial $500 counts as a whole one (KRS 142.050). The clerk does the arithmetic and holds the deed until the tax is paid. Out of what comes in, the clerk keeps 5 percent and sends the remainder to the county treasurer every quarter.

A gift, or a deed that recites only token consideration, is taxed on open-market value. Some transfers owe nothing:

  • Foreclosure, or voluntary surrender under a mortgage.
  • Spouse to spouse, including former spouses dividing property in a divorce.
  • Parent and child, or grandparent and grandchild, for nominal money.
  • Deeds that only secure or release a debt, or correct an earlier deed.
  • Tax-sale conveyances and partitions.

To claim an exemption, use the Exempt Transfer Affidavit, Form 71A245, which is on the clerk's records page.

The same office renews vehicle registrations. Online renewal asks for a title number, a plate number and a credit card, and a VIN lookup shows the prior year's vehicle tax. Voter registration and election results belong to the elections department.

There is also a delinquent-tax lookup called DTax, where you can see whether a parcel is on the unpaid list. The clerk alone fixes the dollar amount owed on any bill when a sale takes place, so treat the screen as a guide.

Forms are grouped as motor vehicle, legal records, elections and delinquent tax. Sellers mostly need the legal records group, which includes the Exempt Transfer Affidavit, a release of a real estate mortgage, a release of a vendor's lien and an affidavit of conversion to real estate.

Deeds and mortgages are indexed in CCLIX back to 1966, and wills and marriages back to 1797. Images of documents from January 2004 forward can mostly be pulled up online, while paper and microfilm reach into the 1700s.

Online searching goes through eCCLIX, which needs an account from the vendor and charges for use. Inside the clerk's office, anyone can read the same indexes and images for free. DocAlert is a free email service: register a name, and each deed or mortgage recorded under it triggers a notice. Owners who live elsewhere or hold rentals can use it to catch a fraudulent filing early.

sections.h2: If the property tax was never paid
sections.html:
On April 15 the sheriff hands every unpaid bill to the clerk. From there the Sheriff's Office lists a 20 percent County Attorney fee and a 10 percent Clerk fee, plus interest of 1 percent a month, on top of the earlier penalties. A sale of the debt to a private buyer can follow in the summer.

Under KRS 134.015(5) the lien can follow the land for up to eleven years regardless of owner, and a title agent will find it. Plan for the payoff to come out of the seller's net. Until April 15 the Sheriff's Office takes payment, at (502) 839-4021.

• Find your own deed and write down its book and page.
  • Get this year's bill and any older balance from the Sheriff.
  • Ask the clerk about any recorded lien or lis pendens.
  • Write in the buyer's mailing address for the tax bill.
  • Prepare the exemption affidavit if one applies.

If the house came to you by inheritance, add two items: the affidavit from the estate's personal representative and, when the land passed by descent, the affidavit of descent, which the clerk lists at a $50 minimum. Bring a checkbook or ask the closing office how it will pay, because the clerk holds the deed until the fees and the transfer tax are paid.

Anyone selling as is can ask for a written cash offer. Recording follows the same steps once a price is agreed.

The county's population is estimated at 25,225 in mid-2025, up from 23,852 in 2020. It touches seven other counties and belongs to the Frankfort micropolitan area. Half of owner-occupied houses are worth more than $225,100, and owners live in 77.6 percent of 9,653 households. Housing units counted in July 2025 came to 10,652. Middle monthly owner cost is $1,391 with a mortgage and $411 without, and middle gross rent is $927. Place names such as Alton, Glensboro, McBrayer and Stringtown don't change where a deed goes: every parcel is recorded in the same Lawrenceburg books.

faqs.q: Do I still record in Lawrenceburg for a house outside the city?
faqs.a: Yes. Anderson County has one clerk, and KRS 382.110 sends a deed to the clerk of the county that holds the land, so a rural parcel goes to the same S Main Street office.

faqs.q: What does the clerk charge at minimum for a deed?
faqs.a: Fifty dollars, with $3 added for each page after the fifth. KRS 142.010 also puts a $4 state tax on conveyances, so ask for the full total first.

faqs.q: Is the seller or the buyer responsible for the transfer tax?
faqs.a: The seller, named as grantor, pays it. KRS 142.050 sets it at half a dollar per $500 of declared value, and the clerk collects it at the counter.
In the office, yes: indexes and records are free to view there. Online viewing through eCCLIX costs money.
No. KRS 142.050 exempts foreclosure transfers and voluntary surrenders under a mortgage. The lender then has 45 days from signing to file that deed with the clerk, under KRS 382.110.
